operator_io_quirks: phone_market.phone_market.Phone_ID is declared TEXT but its FK parent phone.Phone_ID is declared INT and stores integers; child stores text '1'..'4' — declared-type/storage contradiction across an FK edge.
phone_market.phone_market has composite PK (Market_ID, Phone_ID) with both members also FKs to different parents; PK member Phone_ID is TEXT-typed.
All columns are nullable (notnull=0) including PKs; upstream does not enforce NOT NULL, so NULL PK rows will be attempted and skipped at insert.
No CHECK constraints, no UNIQUE indexes beyond PKs; 'checked'/'unique' line-scan will find nothing.
Tiny tables (5, 6, 6 rows) — no rowid sampling needed; original_values fully read.

Table names all lowercase, column names mixed case ('Name', 'Phone_ID', 'Memory_in_G', 'Num_of_employees', 'Num_of_shops', 'Num_of_stock', 'Ranking', 'District', 'Carrier', 'Price') — must be double-quoted with original case.
FK parent columns are PKs (unique) — no non-unique-parent issue here.
No self-references, no dangling FKs, no views/triggers/indexes in DDL.
market.Market_ID samples show 1..5 but distinct=6 (6th value unseen in samples) — original_values must be read fully, not from samples.
phone_market.Market_ID distinct=4 while market has 6 rows — child references only a subset of parents; FK fill must draw from parent's generated values, not assume full coverage.
phone_market.Phone_ID distinct=4 while phone has 5 rows — same subset pattern.
REAL columns (Price, Num_of_shops) store integral floats (320.0, 40.0) — Number fuzzer with scale from 'real' (no args) will produce wide-range floats.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on INT columns (Phone_ID, Memory_in_G, Market_ID, Num_of_employees, Ranking, Num_of_stock): no (a,b) args so scale=0, range [-1,1] for ints — will produce values like -1,0,1,2,3, wildly implausible for Memory_in_G (16..128) or Num_of_stock (hundreds..thousands).
Number fuzzer on REAL columns (Price, Num_of_shops): scale=0 too (no args), range [-1,1] — Price 320..1000 and Num_of_shops 10..54 become ~[-1,1]; strong FN driver for range predicates.
String fuzzer on Name, Carrier, District: charset a-zA-Z 0-9() length 0..20, plus contaminate — will not resemble 'IPhone 5s' or 'British Columbia'; FN for LIKE/equality on these.

String fuzzer on phone_market.Phone_ID (TEXT): will generate random strings, but FK fill overrides with parent phone.Phone_ID values (integers as ints) — type mismatch: child TEXT column receives ints from parent, sqlite stores as int; joins on Phone_ID may still work via affinity but comparisons to text literals may miss.

FK fill: phone_market.Market_ID and Phone_ID drawn with replacement from parent's FINAL filtered values — with tiny parents (5-6 rows) and child size possibly 1..2500, heavy duplication; composite PK dedup then drops most rows, leaving few distinct (Market_ID,Phone_ID) pairs.
choose_table_sizes: level 0 = {phone, market} (no deps), level 1 = {phone_market}; sizes 1+30u and x4 — phone_market may be ~4x parent size, then PK dedup collapses to at most 5*6=30 distinct pairs.
Composite PK member Phone_ID gets max_l0=30 cap; single-column PKs (phone.Phone_ID, market.Market_ID) get inf — parent PKs may generate many fresh values, child FK draws from them.
p=0.2 default, whole-instance p=0 w.p. 0.3 — when p=0, Number/String return elements (original 5 + pool) with perturbation; still implausible for Memory_in_G etc.
Date/Time/Bool/Bit fuzzers unused (no such declared types).

Known misses: FN from implausible numeric ranges (Price, Memory_in_G, Num_of_stock) and random strings (Name, District); FP from missing ties — original has ties (e.g. Carrier 'Sprint'/'TMobile' only 2 distinct, Memory_in_G 4 distinct over 5 rows) but TS may generate all-distinct or all-same values, breaking GROUP BY / DISTINCT / top-k semantics.
